headline: Earnings jump on lower losses, adjusted profit slips
summary_short: Aflac reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $4.12B (-1.0% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.63, up 46.8% y/y as net investment losses shrank sharply, while adjusted EPS fell 1.7% y/y to $1.75.
summary_long: Revenue fell 1.0% y/y to $4.12B, driven by declines in Aflac Japan (weaker yen, a reinsurance transaction) partly offset by 2.5% U.S. growth. GAAP net earnings rose 37.7% y/y to $825M ($1.63 diluted EPS) as net investment losses shrank to $153M from $421M; adjusted earnings, which strip out those swings, fell 7.7% to $883M ($1.75 adjusted EPS) on weaker-yen drag. Shareholders' equity climbed 11.4% y/y to $30.3B, aided by a discount-rate assumption change. Aflac returned $1.3B to shareholders ($983M buybacks, $309M dividends) and declared a $0.61 Q3 dividend.
confidence_notes: Regenerated summary (force-regenerate mode) — this file supersedes any prior version for this ticker/period. GAAP net earnings rose sharply y/y mainly because net investment losses shrank ($153M vs $421M a year ago), not because of stronger underlying insurance operations; adjusted earnings, which exclude those investment swings, actually fell 7.7% y/y — the GAAP ($1.63) and adjusted ($1.75) diluted EPS figures measure different things and should not be compared directly. A 9.3%-weaker yen/dollar rate (159.45 vs 144.60) suppressed Aflac Japan's dollar-translated results and cut $0.05 off adjusted EPS.

drivers.explanation: Aflac Japan premiums fell on a new external reinsurance transaction for WAYS/Tsumitasu and limited-pay products reaching paid-up status, partly offset by 2.5% growth in the U.S. segment.
Net investment losses shrank to $153M from $421M a year ago, including a smaller net loss on sales/redemptions and an $87M fair-value gain on equity securities.
Driven mainly by a $10.4B cumulative discount-rate assumption benefit on insurance reserves, partly offset by a $5.0B foreign-currency translation loss and a $2.8B unrealized investment loss.

Adjusted earnings, which exclude investment-related swings, fell 7.7% y/y as the weaker yen cut $0.05 from adjusted EPS — the release treats this as the better read on underlying insurance profitability than the GAAP jump.
